project_metadata.job_description:
I have my own brand for male enhancement product which we promote on Social Media. We need video ads for the same product. 

I have attached a sample video which was created by me but i need better video quality. 

Only those must apply who think they can bring sales through their video. They must have deep knowledge about the category we are working in specifically indian market. Video needs to be created in Hindi.

messages.speaker: client

messages.text: If you can identify the reason why 3rd one is not performing than you can certainly create a winning creative. I am only looking for an expert who can provide me a winning creative which can provide me cpl below 50inr.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I ran all three through a frame by frame and audio analysis. Here is what I found.

First, something you need to know before anything else. Your two performing creatives are the same video.

newvid.mp4 is 1080x1080 at 3.1 Mbps. Purushveda\_Herbs is 720x720 at 550 kbps. Same scene cut timestamps to the frame, same audio mean volume of 17.3 dB, same peak of 1.0 dB, same silence points at 23.2s and 29.2s. The second file is simply Meta's compressed download of the first one after it went live.

So you do not have two winners and one loser. You have one winner and one loser. Your winning pattern is a sample of one, which is why the third one is hard to diagnose from the outside.

Now, why the third one failed.

1\. It is not a video. It is a static image with subtitles.

Your winner has 14 scene cuts across 30 seconds, an average shot length of 2.1 seconds, and its first cut lands at 2.0 seconds.

The failing one has 1 cut across 32.6 seconds. It holds a single image for the first 21.8 seconds, then cuts once to a static product card and holds that for the last 11 seconds.

Motion is what buys the hold. Meta measures the 3 second view, and your winner cuts at 2.0 seconds, right before that gate. The failing creative gives the viewer nothing to watch at second 2, second 5 or second 15. There is nothing to stop the scroll and nothing to sustain attention once stopped.

2\. The audio is 9 dB quieter and it stalls eight times.

Winner: mean volume 17.3 dB, peak 1.0 dB, two pauses in 30 seconds.
Failing: mean volume 26.2 dB, peak 9.0 dB, eight silence gaps in 32.6 seconds.

Same voice in both, so this is a mixing and editing problem, not a voice problem. A 9 dB gap is roughly half the perceived loudness on a phone. On top of that, the failing creative goes silent eight separate times with no music bed underneath it. It sounds quiet and it sounds hesitant.

3\. It opens on the outcome instead of the problem.

Frame one is the happy result the product promises. There is no tension and no curiosity gap, so there is no reason to keep watching. Your winner opens on a situation, not a conclusion.

There is a fourth issue that applies to all three. Every one of them is 1:1 square. That forfeits Reels and Stories placements entirely and gives away vertical space in feed. Your next creative should ship 9:16 as primary and 4:5 as secondary.

On what I will build.

Not one video. Three distinct angles built on the structural rules your winner already proves, delivered in 9:16 and 4:5, so you have something real to test instead of a single creative and a hope. Single creatives do not produce winners consistently. Tested angles do.

On your 50 INR CPL target. I will be straight with you because it is worth more to you than agreement. Creative controls hook rate, hold rate and CTR. CPL is set by creative, offer, landing page and bidding together. Anyone who guarantees you a CPL number from a video alone is guessing. What I will commit to is beating your current winner on hook rate and hold rate, and I will show you the numbers.

To target this properly, send me the hook rate, hold rate, link CTR and landing page conversion rate for the winner. That tells me where your ceiling actually is.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I went through the data. A few things stand out.

Your cost per lead is ₹76.52 against your ₹50 target, so the account is running 53% over goal. But the breakdown shows this isn't purely a creative problem.

Link CTR is 3.54%, genuinely strong, so the ad itself is earning attention fine. The real leak is right after the click: only 59.7% of link clicks are registering as landing page views, meaning roughly 40% of paid clicks are dropping before the page even loads for tracking. That's a page speed or tracking setup issue, not a video issue, and no creative fixes that.

More importantly, your Quality Ranking is Below Average, bottom 35%, while Engagement Rate and Conversion Rate are both Above Average. That combination usually means the ad or landing page experience is triggering negative signals (hidden ads, reports) even though people who click are converting fine. Left alone, that quietly inflates your CPMs across the account regardless of how strong the next creative is.

So here's where I'd focus to actually hit ₹50 CPL, not just a better video:

1\. New creative built on the structural rules your winner proves, faster cuts, corrected audio levels, proper hook, shipped in 9:16 and 4:5
2\. A check on landing page load speed and pixel/tracking setup, since that 40% drop-off is costing real budget independent of the ad. I can take a look at this directly if useful, tracking and funnel issues like this are part of what I handle on the automation side of my work, not just video
3\. Monitoring Quality Ranking after the fix, since that's the number that tells us whether the negative feedback issue is resolving

If this direction makes sense, I'll put together a quote and timeline for the creative rebuild, plus a note on the landing page fix if you'd like me to take that on too. Let me know and I'll send it over.

For this project, my recommendation is to generate native-looking AI video scenes where the product is naturally handled and the motion feels like real UGC. Static-image animation can work for certain use cases, but for a performance campaign like this, it usually doesn't create the level of realism needed to maximize watch time and engagement.
